narrative.overview:
The tournament reads like a Turkish sports fixture sheet: big condensed headlines, numbers as the heroes, matches as versus rows, and content grouped by horizontal rules rather than boxed in nested cards. Every public page (landing, teams, qualifiers, bracket list, team page) is a stack of ruled sections under a heavy-ruled headline, with dense rows on hairlines beneath. The admin side keeps boxed tool panels where a tool genuinely needs a container (the referee page, the map pool editor, the bracket board), but its page headers follow the same sheet.

The sheet is printed in the world of the designers' first banner (`design/bannertest.png`, "112'nin Son Kış Turnuvası", still a test version): a cold slate ground, frost-white ink, and the icy glow of the tournament's mark, an ice crystal drawn with the digits 1, 1 and 2. The banner also lends the page its atmosphere (faint gear linework in two corners and a film of grain, behind the content) and the wordmark its voice (the display face expanded and light). The artwork is the designers'; the site uses what was cut from it and invents none of its own.

Density is high and calm: a 16px body, a dense 4px-based spacing scale, rows of about 60px, and a 1440px content width. Motion is limited to short colour and background transitions on hover and focus.
keyCharacteristics: Hecate Display, a high-contrast condensed display serif, by role: every title and heading, stage names, team names, player names, map names, bracket match codes (W12, L3) and the top bar's links and buttons (and the wordmark, the banner's line in its italic, team monograms).

Helvetica Neue LT Pro for everything else: normal width for body, controls and map details (difficulty, mapper, stats); condensed for every score, time, countdown, code, value and count, with tabular digits; extended for the overlay's numbers.
A heavy ink rule opens each page and section; hairline rules separate rows.
Team red and team blue structure every head-to-head; one frost accent marks live, yours, current and the primary action.
Slate ground with gear linework and grain behind the content; the trophy mark in the nav and favicon; the banner as the landing hero.
Every colour is a role token taken from the test banner, so the final banner is a value swap.

rules.name: The Banner Palette Rule
rules.body: The palette comes from the designers' test banner, and every colour is still consumed by role only: components reference role tokens (`--color-*`, `--rule*`, `--glow` in `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`), and a raw colour value in a component stylesheet is a defect (mask gradients, which carry only alpha, are the exception). When the final banner arrives: (1) change the values in `tokens.css` only, keeping every role name; (2) keep `on-brand` legible on `brand` (frost is a light fill, so it takes slate ink); (3) keep team red and team blue distinguishable from each other and from `brand` and `danger` (both are light fills on the public site, so a solid side fill takes slate ink); (4) re-export the assets from the final banner as `frontend/src/assets/README.md` describes, keeping the file names; (5) re-run the document pass so this file and its sidecar record the new values. Soft variants (`brand-soft`, `team-*-soft`, `danger-soft`) are the base colour at 12–18% alpha, and several components derive tints with `color-mix()` from the base team and brand colours, so they follow automatically.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Frost appears only for live, yours, current position, the single primary action and the wordmark's year. It never decorates a heading, a divider or a category.

rules.name: The Strong Yours Rule
rules.body: Frost sits close to the ink, so "yours" is never carried by a wash alone: an own team name is frost at 700, an own lobby title frost at 900, and an own bracket row that is hovered steps to a deeper frost wash (10%) so hover never reads as just "yours".

rules.name: The Sides Rule
rules.body: Any time two teams face each other, team 1 is blue and team 2 is red (the room's slots 1-2 and 3-4; green and purple on the public site, osu!'s own blue and red on the referee page and the players' room page), and both colours appear. A head-to-head without its side colours is incomplete.

rules.name: The Naming Rule
rules.body: Hecate is for what something is called; Helvetica is for everything said about it. Never set a quantity in Hecate (a score, time, count or value), and never set a title, a match code, a team, a player, a stage or a map standing on its own in Helvetica. A match code is the match's name, so it is Hecate though it holds a number. One exception: on the public Mappool page the slot labels (NM1, HD2…) are Hecate, as the categories' own headings are; everywhere else a slot label is a figure.

rules.name: The Size Floor
rules.body: Hecate's hairlines need room: a name is never set under 14px, and small Hecate names are one step larger than the Helvetica text beside them.

rules.name: The Ruled Sheet Rule
rules.body: Content is grouped by rules, not boxes: `--rule-heavy` (3px ink) under page and section headings and over each lobby and team block; `--rule` (1px hairline) between rows. Public pages prefer ruled lists over bordered cards. Admin tool panels may keep boxes.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: A row, a section or a team block never takes a shadow. If it needs separation, it gets a rule.

rules.name: The Lit Things Rule
rules.body: The crystal's glow is the one sanctioned exception to the flat sheet and to zero-offset halos, earned by the banner: it is allowed only on the live dot and on the current stage's rule on the stage track. A button, a card, a heading or the primary action never glows.

dos: **Do** reference role tokens from `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` for every colour, size, radius and timing.
**Do** take the palette from the designers' banner and swap it by changing values in `tokens.css` while keeping role names; re-export the assets per `frontend/src/assets/README.md`.

**Do** set titles, stage names, team names, player names, map names, match codes and the top bar in Hecate Display, and every score, time, countdown and value in condensed Helvetica Neue with tabular figures.
**Do** keep Hecate's italic for the banner's line.
**Do** group public content with a heavy rule under headings and over blocks, and hairlines between rows.
**Do** show both team colours in every head-to-head: team 1 blue, team 2 red.
**Do** reuse the fixture row for any list of matches.
**Do** mark the viewer's own team, lobby or row with frost ink at full weight, a frost rule or the frost wash, never the wash alone on a name.
**Do** show disabled primary buttons as grey (surface-raised, subtle ink), not as a dimmed frost fill.
**Do** feather the banner into the ground rather than framing it.
donts: **Don't** invent artwork, illustration or a new mark; use only what the designers supplied, in the places listed under Atmosphere and artwork.
**Don't** put the glow on anything but the live dot and the current stage.
**Don't** use frost for decoration, headings, dividers or categories; it means live, yours, current or primary.
**Don't** box public lists in same-size bordered cards or nest boxes inside boxes; use rules.
**Don't** put shadows on rows, sections or blocks, or let the gear linework and grain into a surface.
**Don't** set a number in Hecate, a name under 14px, or ask Hecate for a weight it doesn't have to tell two things apart.
**Don't** add small uppercase tracked labels above headings or fields; let the heading and the value carry the hierarchy.
